quizName: DMV Practice Test #4 20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: What should boots or shoes do to protect a motorcycle rider?

options.text: Have long laces that hang loose.
Cover the ankle and provide support.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover the ankle and provide support.
questions.explanation: Choose boots or heavy shoes that cover and support your ankles. Heels should be low so they don't catch on surfaces. Tuck in long laces so they don't catch on the motorcycle's moving parts.

questions.question: Your friend has had too much to drink and wants to ride their motorcycle. What should you do?

options.text: Tell them to take quiet roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take their keys.
questions.explanation: Never allow someone to ride if they have been drinking. Stop them from riding by taking their keys if needed. Help arrange another way for them to get home.

questions.question: What is a benefit of smoothly downshifting on a motorcycle?

options.text: It allows the rider to use engine braking.
It should not be done near other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: It allows the rider to use engine braking.
questions.explanation: Smoothly downshifting can help you use engine braking. When you engine brake, use your brake lights separately to alert other drivers that you are slowing down.

questions.question: Which surface is slippery and makes it hard to control a motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: Wet pavement
questions.explanation: Slippery surfaces include wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal covers in the road. Ride with extra care on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: What should you do when riding with a passenger?

options.text: Assume they have ridden a motorcycle before.
Do not assume they have ridden before. Explain what to do.
Do not let them ask questions.
Do not explain anything since they are just a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not assume they have ridden before. Explain what to do.
questions.explanation: Passengers need to know how to stay safe. Never assume a passenger knows what to do. Give them complete instructions before every ride.

questions.question: How can you reduce your risk of crashing?

options.text: Tell other drivers your plans with signals and lights.
Ride in spots where others can't see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell other drivers your plans with signals and lights.
questions.explanation: Stay visible to other drivers. Use signals, brake lights, and smart lane position to show what you plan to do. Keep space around your motorcycle and always watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: What is the best footwear for a motorcycle operator?
questions.correctAnswerText: Sturdy boots
questions.explanation: Sturdy boots or high shoes that support your ankles provide the best protection. Laced-up boots are ideal. If you wear shoes with long laces, tuck them in securely before riding.

questions.question: How should you ride when carrying a passenger?

options.text: Try to fit into smaller spaces in traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride more slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight that changes how your motorcycle handles. It will accelerate slower, turn slower, and need more distance to stop. Ride more slowly, start slowing sooner, keep a bigger space around you, and wait for larger gaps when turning or merging.

questions.question: When passing parked vehicles, what should motorcycle riders watch for?

options.text: Cars pulling out of parking spaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cars pulling out of parking spaces.
questions.explanation: Be careful when passing parked vehicles. Vehicles may pull out from the curb or parking spaces.

questions.question: If your motorcycle will take longer to stop than usual, what should you do?

options.text: Stay farther behind the vehicle ahead.
Stay closer behind the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther behind the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: Stay farther behind other vehicles on slippery surfaces. If your motorcycle needs more distance to stop, keep a longer distance between you and the vehicle ahead.

questions.question: For the best protection, wear a helmet that:
questions.correctAnswerText: Fits snugly.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. It should fit snugly all the way around with no obvious defects.

questions.question: If you ride on the right side of your lane while following a car:

options.text: You are likely riding in the best position to be seen.
You may not be seen unless the driver uses their side mirror.
The driver will most likely assume you are there.
You are discouraging other drivers from sharing your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not be seen unless the driver uses their side mirror.
questions.explanation: When riding behind a car, ride in the center of the lane. This position is visible in the driver's rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirrors much more often than their side mirrors, so this helps other drivers see you.

questions.question: Riding at night:

options.text: Is made safer by wearing reflective clothing.
Is not safe because other drivers cannot see your turn signals.
Should only be done in the city.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is made safer by wearing reflective clothing.
questions.explanation: Wear reflective materials when riding at night. This makes you more visible to other drivers.

questions.question: In a no passing zone:

options.text: A motorcycle may still pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle is not allowed to pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle may pass another vehicle if the pass can be completed before another vehicle approaches.
A motorcycle may pass on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle is not allowed to pass another vehicle.
questions.explanation: Passing is not allowed in no passing zones. You cannot pass by riding off the main part of the road either.

questions.question: As a motorcycle rider, you can help others see you by:
questions.correctAnswerText: Wearing bright clothing.
questions.explanation: To be more visible, wear bright clothing, keep your headlight on at all times, and always use your turn signals.

questions.question: What is often found in the center of the lane?
questions.correctAnswerText: An oily or greasy strip
questions.explanation: Oil and grease from cars form a strip in the center of each lane. Unless the road is wet, it is usually still safe for a motorcycle to ride on this center strip.

questions.question: A face shield:

options.text: Provides protection for the eyes and face.
Does not protect the face as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Provides protection for the eyes and face.
questions.explanation: A plastic, impact-resistant face shield provides the best protection for your eyes and face. Regular eyeglasses or sunglasses are not enough. In Vermont, you do not need eye or face protection if your motorcycle has a windshield, but it is still recommended.

questions.question: To reduce your chances of an accident, you should:

options.text: Ride within a foot of the vehicle in front of you.
Signal only when you feel like it.
Stay alert and be ready to avoid a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay alert and be ready to avoid a crash.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, stay visible to others. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position to show your intentions. Keep space around your motorcycle and watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: An approved helmet:

options.text: Allows the wearer to see as far to the sides as necessary.
Does not have any markings or tags.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allows the wearer to see as far to the sides as necessary.
questions.explanation: An approved helmet lets you see as far to the sides as you need for safe riding. Approved helmets have labels and markings that show the manufacturer's name, instructions, and which safety standards they meet.

questions.question: The best way to keep a group of riders together is to:

options.text: Ride on the shoulder of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in a staggered formation.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation lets riders stay close together while keeping safe space around each motorcycle. Switch to single-file formation when turning, in curves, entering a highway, or exiting a highway.
